package_info.package_versions: Affected versions distributed after build environment compromise (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The 3CX desktop client was compromised in the software supply chain by state-sponsored attackers, who tampered with the build environment and injected a backdoor into the signed application, which was then distributed to customers as a legitimate update.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after installation and execution of the desktop client)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into the main application binary of the 3CX desktop client (Windows/macOS)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Backdoor code injected into the 3CX desktop client binary (exact code not shown in report, but described as a backdoor enabling remote access and command execution).
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++/C#/Objective-C (depending on platform, not specified in report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code establishes a connection to a remote command-and-control server, receives instructions, and can execute arbitrary commands or exfiltrate data from the host system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is not part of the legitimate application logic and enables remote control by unauthorized parties.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal desktop client software should not include hidden remote access or command execution capabilities.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools may have similar capabilities, but only with explicit user consent and transparency.
key_indicators: Injected code not present in original source

attack_chain.action: State-sponsored attackers compromise the 3CX build environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is injected into the desktop client.

attack_chain.action: Malicious backdoor code is added to the 3CX desktop client binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromised application is signed and distributed to customers.

attack_chain.action: Customers install the signed, but compromised, 3CX desktop client.
Backdoor establishes connection to attacker infrastructure and enables remote access.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential data exfiltration, lateral movement, or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from desktop client processes
Execution of code not present in official source repositories
Presence of remote command execution capabilities in non-remote-support software
file_indicators: Modified or anomalous 3CX desktop client binaries
Unexpected changes in signed application hashes
network_indicators: Connections to known command-and-control domains associated with the 3CX compromise
Unusual traffic patterns from desktop client applications
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for changes in the hash or digital signature of the 3CX desktop client binaries, analyze network traffic for connections to suspicious domains, and inspect running processes for unexpected remote access or command execution behavior. Compare deployed binaries against known-good versions and investigate any discrepancies.
